title: Using Images in Presentations Without the Clutter (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Using Images Without the Clutter
slides.notes: Most decks have too many pictures, too small, placed wherever there was room. The fix isn't design talent. It's a few simple rules.

slides.title: Ask One Question Before Adding Images
bullets: What would the viewer lose without it?
A screenshot of the actual product
A photo of the real place, team or object
slides.notes: Before adding any image, ask what the viewer would lose if it were gone. If the answer is nothing, leave it out.

slides.title: Choose Fewer, Bigger, Well-Cropped Pictures
bullets: One strong image at full width
Crop to the button, field or chart
Faces on the upper third line
slides.notes: One strong image at full width beats three small ones. Then crop away anything that doesn't support the point.

slides.title: Keep Text Off Busy Areas
bullets: Text over sky, a plain wall or blur
Or add a dark or light band
Aim for 4.5:1 contrast, 3:1 for large text
slides.notes: Pick one layout per slide. If a headline sits over a photo, find the quiet part, or add a contrast band behind it.

slides.title: One Image, One Claim, One Line
bullets: Before: four stamp-sized photos, eight features
After: one large photo of the Trail Pack
Other products moved to their own slides
slides.notes: Four tiny product photos became one large shot of the Trail Pack. One image, one claim, one sentence of support. The narration does the rest.

slides.title: Clean Images Make Better Video
bullets: A slow zoom on static photos
Images arrive as the narration mentions them
Leave the bottom calm for captions
slides.notes: Fewer, bigger images make a better video. On Pro, a.i. directs it, framing each picture as a scene timed to your voice. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
